# Feature: LLM-Assisted Workflow Replay

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-FP-001
**Source**: Plan Feature agent (self-contained — no plan file)

`yantra run <workflow>` executes a saved workflow deterministically and, today, reports whatever
raw text the recorded `extract` step happened to scrape. The same task run as `yantra do` ends in a
synthesized, citation-backed Brief. A workflow promoted from `do --save-as` therefore _loses_ the
document that made the original run useful: [promote.ts](../../packages/core/src/discovery/promote.ts)
collapses the trailing read into one `extract` of `body` and binds `capture.X.rows[0]` to an output,
discarding the published Brief entirely.

This feature closes that gap. `yantra run` gains a post-execution **Synthesize stage** that produces
the same `brief.json` / `brief.md` / `brief.html` artifacts `ask`, `research`, and `do` produce — by
reusing the existing `packages/core/src/synthesis/` stage rather than inventing a second one.

The stage runs in **both** modes, and **the workflow — not the invocation — selects which**
(amended 2026-07-30; see §9):

- **`synthesis.use_llm: false`** (the default, and every workflow saved before the field existed) —
  `DeterministicSynthesizer` produces a real, schema-valid Brief. Replay stays byte-for-byte
  deterministic and opens no provider session.
- **`synthesis.use_llm: true`** (what `do --save-as` records) — `LlmSynthesizer` produces a
  citation-validated Brief, with a bounded re-prompt loop and an automatic fall back to the
  deterministic strategy on any failure.

`yantra run` therefore carries **no opt-in mode flag**; `--no-llm` is a veto only. So "with or
without LLM" is not "document vs. raw dump" — it is "synthesized document, richer or plainer". The
LLM upgrades quality; it never gates whether the run produces a document.

## 2. Technical Context

> Standing rules live in [`.spec-lite/memory.md`](../memory.md). Only additions and overrides appear here.

### Approach

**Reuse the Synthesize stage; do not build a second one.** `packages/core/src/synthesis/` already
contains `Synthesizer`, `DeterministicSynthesizer`, `LlmSynthesizer` (citation validation + bounded
re-prompt + deterministic fallback), and `selectSynthesizer`, whose documented selection rules are
already exactly this feature's requirement:

> 1. `--no-llm` → deterministic (the agent-optional invariant). … 3. No LLM port wired → deterministic.

`SynthesisInput` maps onto replay almost field-for-field, including `scope: 'public' | 'read-only-data'
| 'authenticated'` — the identical value space of a workflow's `security_class`.

Three seams are **specified but unimplemented** in the codebase today. This feature fills them in as
the original architecture intended:

1. **`SynthesisLlm`** — no production implementation exists. Built in `apps/cli` over the existing
   `AgentProvider` seam: open one session with **zero tools** and use it as a completion endpoint
   (run prompt → accumulate `assistant_text` deltas → close). No new SDK dependency, no new auth path,
   and it reuses `--provider` / `--model` / `--thinking` / `--auth-secret` from
   [agent-model.ts](../../apps/cli/src/agent-model.ts) verbatim.
2. **`SynthesisPromptTemplate`** — no implementation exists.
   [types.ts:293](../../packages/core/src/synthesis/types.ts#L293) already names its intended home:
   `packages/agent/src/synthesis/prompt.ts`. Prompt text lives agent-side and is injected as data.
3. **Replay evidence ledger** — `extract` currently discards the page URL, so a Brief would have no
   citable sources. Extract steps record `{url, host, title, text, fetchedAt}` into the execution context.

Brief **sources stay engine-owned**, mirroring `result_publish`'s ledger-authoritative rule: the model
authors prose (title / overview / findings / sections) and never couriers URLs.

### The relaxed determinism invariant

Memory currently states replay is _"finite, validated, deterministic, and LLM-free"_. Per user
decision (2026-07-28) this is **restated**, not discarded:

> Saved workflow replay is finite, validated, and **LLM-free by default**. An LLM may **transform a
> declared capture or synthesize the run's output document** — it may **never steer replay**: not step
> selection, not branch conditions, not loop bounds, not locator repair. Plan shape is fixed and
> validated before execution and cannot change based on model output.

The removed **"task-shaped `LLMClient` scaffolding"** the Dependencies rule bans (`packages/agent/src/client/*`,
`generatePlan()`, generated LLM step catalogs) was a model _planning the task_. That remains banned and
is untouched here. TASK-009 updates memory to this wording.

Guarantees that must survive verbatim:

- Scheduled / daemon runs are **hard zero-LLM**, regardless of flags.
- Nested `workflow_run` invocations from an agent are **hard zero-LLM**.
- The existing real-Chrome e2e ("a promoted workflow replays green with no LLM") stays green unmodified.

### Spec-Specific Overrides

- **Memory → Architecture**: the "LLM-free replay" clause is amended as quoted above. Justification: an
  `llm_summarize` step and a `synthesis:` block are declared, validated leaves in a finite plan — the
  plan shape cannot change based on model output, so the determinism guarantee the rule protects is
  preserved. TASK-009 lands the memory edit.
- **Scope spill (approved)**: TASK-002 adds a file under `packages/agent/` even though the feature is
  about `run`. Required by the layering rule — `core` must never import `agent`, so prompt text must
  live agent-side and be injected as data. Side benefit: it also unblocks `ask`'s deterministic-pipeline
  LLM synthesis, currently dead for exactly this missing piece.
- **No new third-party dependency.** Memory requires checking before pinning one; this feature needs none.

## 3. Data Model (Granular)

No relational data model. Three structural additions:

### `WorkflowSynthesis` (new, protocol) — optional top-level workflow block

- `goal` (string, min 1) — the question/topic the Brief answers; becomes `SynthesisInput.query`.
- `length` (`'short' | 'medium' | 'long'`, default `'medium'`) — findings/sections budget.
- `detail` (`'overview' | 'standard' | 'full'`, default `'standard'`) — Brief depth.
- `use_llm` (boolean, default `false`) — whether a model writes the Brief. **The only thing that can
  opt a replay into a provider session** (§9). Set by promotion from a model-authored run.

Added to `WorkflowFile` as `synthesis: WorkflowSynthesis | null`, `.default(null)`. **Optional by
construction** — every existing workflow parses unchanged and behaves exactly as today.

### `ReplayEvidenceEntry` (new, core) — one recorded source read

- `url` (string) — `ctx.page.url()` at extract time.
- `finalUrl` (string | null) — post-redirect URL when observed, else null.
- `host` (string) — derived from `finalUrl ?? url`.
- `title` (string | null) — `document.title`, null when unavailable.
- `text` (string) — the extracted text (readable output, or serialized rows for a table).
- `fetchedAt` (ISO-8601) — from `ctx.clock.now()`, **not** wall time, so artifacts stay reproducible.
- `stepId` (string) — the originating extract step, for audit join.

### Extensions to existing types

- `ExecutionContext.evidence: ReplayEvidenceLedger | null` — append-only; null in contexts that don't collect.
- `TranslatedWorkflow.synthesisSpec: WorkflowSynthesis | null`.
- `RunManifest.synthesis?: { strategy: 'deterministic' | 'llm'; fallbackUsed: boolean; briefPath: string | null }`.
- `OrchestratorRunOutcome` (`kind: 'success'`) gains `brief?: { jsonPath; mdPath; htmlPath }`.

### Constraints

- `ReplayEvidenceLedger` is capped (**32 entries**, **256 KB** total text) — replay loops can extract
  thousands of times and an unbounded ledger would blow both memory and the prompt budget. Overflow
  drops oldest-first and records a `BriefNotice`.
- `synthesis.goal` is capped at 512 chars at schema level.

## 7. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: Model credentials reuse `selectAgentAuth` — `managed` by default, `--auth-secret <ref>` for a
  runtime-only keychain key. No new credential path, no credential persisted in run artifacts.
- **Sanitization**: Every payload reaching the model passes `sanitize(text, profileFor(scope), host)` inside
  `LlmSynthesizer` before `llm.send(...)`, enforced by the CI static check
  (`scripts/ci-static-check.ts`). The scope is the workflow's `security_class`, so an `authenticated`
  workflow gets the strict profile. `llm_summarize` retains its existing `ctx.sanitizer.sanitize()` call.
- **Error Handling**: Synthesis is **best-effort throughout** — a provider failure, malformed model output
  that never validates, or an artifact-write failure degrades to the deterministic Brief or to no Brief, and
  never converts a successful run into a failed one. Exit codes are unchanged (0/1/2/3/4). `SynthesisLlm`
  returns typed `Result` errors and never throws. Invalid `--provider`/`--model` remains a **validation**
  failure (exit 1), resolved before execution begins.
- **Logging**: Structured Pino only. Log strategy selected, fallback used, token/cost usage, and ledger
  overflow count. Never log prompt bodies, extracted page text, or resolved secrets. `manifest.synthesis`
  records provenance; the run directory stays the durable observability artifact.
- **Budgets**: The LLM path is one call plus at most `DEFAULT_MAX_REPROMPTS` (2) retries — bounded by
  construction. The evidence-ledger caps bound prompt size.
- **Determinism**: With no `--llm`, replay opens no provider session and remains byte-for-byte reproducible
  (timestamps come from the injected clock).

## 9. Amendment (2026-07-30): the workflow declares the mode, not the flag

`--llm` was an opt-in mode flag no sibling command had. `ask`, `research`, and `do` all produce their
normal output with no mode flag; requiring one on `run` meant a workflow promoted from `yantra do`
silently produced a plainer document than the run it came from until the user remembered `--llm`.
Consistent CLI UX is a standing Yantra requirement (`.spec-lite/memory.md` → General), so the mode
moved into the artifact.

**What changed**

| Before                                    | After                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `yantra run wf --llm`                     | `yantra run wf` — the workflow's `synthesis.use_llm` decides             |
| `--llm` opt-in + `--no-llm` veto          | `--no-llm` veto only; no opt-in flag exists                              |
| Model flags inert without `--llm`         | Model flags choose _which_ model a declaring workflow gets               |
| Promotion recorded `synthesis.goal`       | Promotion also records `use_llm: true` (the agent authored that Brief)   |
| `strategies.noLlm` was the whole decision | Decision is `spec.useLlm && !strategies.noLlm` — a veto can never opt in |

**Files touched beyond §4**: `packages/protocol/src/schemas/workflow.ts` (`use_llm`),
`packages/core/src/workflow/replay/synthesize.ts` (`SynthesisSpec.useLlm`, `toSynthesisSpec`,
construction-failure fallback), `packages/core/src/discovery/promote.ts` (`synthesisUsedLlm`),
`packages/agent/src/runtime/orchestrator.ts`, `apps/cli/src/commands/run.ts`,
`apps/cli/src/commands/resume.ts`, plus regenerated `docs/protocol-spec.md` and
`packages/protocol/generated/json-schema/workflow.json`.

**Fallback hardening.** `LlmSynthesizer` already fell back on provider/validation failure. The
uncovered case was the strategy _factory_ throwing — before any synthesizer exists — which failed the
whole run. `synthesizeRun` now contains that, and reports `fallbackUsed: true` whenever a workflow
asked for a model and could not have one, so `manifest.synthesis` stays honest and `resume` re-offers
the model instead of inheriting a transient downgrade.

**Guarantees preserved verbatim**: scheduled/daemon runs and nested `workflow_run` stay hard
zero-LLM (they pass `noLlm: true` / `synthesis: null`, which the veto rule makes unconditional); an
`authenticated` `security_class` still stays deterministic via `selectSynthesizer`; the real-Chrome
promotion e2e still replays green with no LLM.
